Subject: Marketplace onboarding — evidence & billing questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement ran through the marketplace checklist and we have a few outstanding clarifications before we can proceed to the vendor acceptance step across our cloud teams (GCP + AWS):

1) Evidence: Procurement asked for a short set of artifacts they can attach to their vendor folder — SOC2 attestation (or summary), data flow diagram showing where customer data transits/keeps KV cache, and a statement on retention defaults.

2) Technical dependencies: Our cloud engineering team flagged questions about KMS/HSM support, private deployment options, and whether your marketplace listing requires any networking peering or VPC connectors for the GCP listing.

3) Billing & SKU mapping: We need an example of how Redwood maps marketplace SKUs to Redwood product SKUs and a sample invoice flow (who bills whom, taxes, and how credits/commits are represented).

Can you provide a short deck or single PDF with the above items and any suggested next steps (e.g., a technical onboarding call with marketplace ops)? We are hoping to close vendor acceptance by April 10.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Cho

Hi Alex —

Thanks, really helpful list. Attaching a consolidated onboarding evidence PDF and a billing SKU mapping CSV to start. Quick notes inline below and we can follow up with a short call to walk GCP/AWS specific nuances: 

- SOC2: We attached a SOC2 summary (public) and can provide the full report under NDA.
- Data flow: Redwood runs ephemeral KV caches for prefix caching. Default retention for hosted API caches is 30 days; customers can request shorter or opt out. Private deployments are customer-controlled.
- KMS/HSM: We support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and have an HSM-friendly workflow for enterprise private deployments.
- GCP marketplace specifics: GCP does not allow direct VPC peering for SaaS listings — most customers use a connector or private service connect. We'll outline options on the call.
- Billing: Attached CSV shows SKU map; Redwood typically invoices customers directly for hosted usage when using our hosted plan, while marketplace purchases (reserved capacity) flow through the marketplace billing pipeline. We included a flow diagram for the two cases.

Next steps: can your team do a 30-minute sync on Thu (Apr 3) or Mon (Apr 7)? If those don't work, propose alternatives and we'll loop in marketplace ops.

Attachments: redwood_marketplace_onboarding_evidence.pdf, billing-sku-mapping.csv

Best,

Tessa — quick answers below; attaching SOC2-Summary-2027.pdf and a short artifacts checklist.

1) SOC2: Public summary is safe to share (we put that in the onboarding PDF). Full SOC2 report is available under NDA; procurement teams typically request a copy for vendor files — we can route through legal.

2) Data retention & PII: Hosted runtime: ephemeral KV caches default to 30 days; we have strict access controls and no customer prompt text is indexed for search. For regulated customers we offer shorter retention windows and can disable caching. Private deployments: retention and logging are customer-configured. We do not use customer prompts for model fine-tuning.

3) KMS/HSM: Supported. Hosted customers may integrate their cloud KMS keys (AWS/GCP/Azure) for service-level encryption; enterprise private deployments have a documented HSM integration path (customer-managed keys).

4) Marketplace nuances: GCP marketplace commonly expects a statement that there is no unauthorized data exfiltration and that billing metadata is separated from customer content. We'll include that language in the response. Also note: GCP SaaS listings rarely support direct VPC peering — we recommend Private Service Connect or connector approaches for network-restricted customers.

Attachments: SOC2-Summary-2027.pdf, onboarding-artifacts-checklist.docx

-Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the list — please find consolidated answers and attachments below. We can take a 30-minute technical onboarding with marketplace ops to walk the networking and billing flows; proposed windows: Thu Apr 3 10:00-10:30 PT or Mon Apr 7 13:00-13:30 PT.

Consolidated answers (short):
- SOC2: Attached SOC2-Summary-2027.pdf (public). Full report available under NDA; contact legal@redwood.ai to request.
- Data flow & retention: Redwood uses ephemeral KV prefix caches for performance. Default retention 30 days for hosted; private deployments are customer-controlled. No customer content is used for model training.
- KMS/HSM: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault and have an HSM integration path for private deployments.
- GCP-specific network: GCP marketplace does not permit direct SaaS VPC peering in most listings; recommended approaches are Private Service Connect or a connector. We'll have a short appendix on the call with sample architectures.
- Billing & SKUs: See attached billing-sku-mapping.csv and billing-flow-diagram.png. For hosted plans Redwood invoices directly. For reserved capacity purchased through a marketplace, billing typically flows through the marketplace with a delay of one billing cycle; taxes and commitments are handled by the marketplace platform per their standard terms.

Attachments: redwood_marketplace_onboarding_evidence.pdf; SOC2-Summary-2027.pdf; billing-sku-mapping.csv; billing-flow-diagram.png

Next steps: 1) Pick one of the proposed meeting slots and we'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda (networking, KMS options, billing mapping). 2) If procurement needs the full SOC2 report we can start an NDA routing.

Best regards,
